Part 1: PCR Reaction Assembly

    Step 1.1: Assemble PCR reactions for Normal Allele ($\beta^{\mathrm{A}}$) detection.

        Option 1.1.1: Reaction Mix for Normal Allele-Specific Amplification.
            - Component A: KCl
                - Recipe: Final concentration of 50 mM.
            - Component B: Tris HCl
                - Recipe: Final concentration of 10 mM, pH 8.3.
            - Component C: MgCl₂
                - Recipe: Final concentration of 1.5 mM.
            - Component D: Gelatin
                - Recipe: Final concentration of 0.01% (wt/vol).
            - Component E: dNTPs (dATP, dCTP, dGTP, TTP)
                - Recipe: Final concentration of 0.1 mM of each nucleoside triphosphate.
            - Component F: HPβ14A
                - Recipe: Final concentration of 0.12 µM.
            - Component G: BGP2
                - Recipe: Final concentration of 0.12 µM.
            - Component H: GHPCR1
                - Recipe: Final concentration of 0.2 µM.
            - Component I: GHPCR2
                - Recipe: Final concentration of 0.2 µM.
            - Component J: *Taq* DNA polymerase
            - Component K: Template DNA / Control
                - Recipe: Added to a final concentration of 0.5 µg/ml for DNA samples. For the reagent control, water is added instead of DNA.
            (Operational details: Prepare a master mix containing components A-J and water, sufficient for the number of reactions. Aliquot the master mix into individual reaction tubes. Add the appropriate Template DNA or water (for reagent control) to each tube to bring the total volume to 50 µl. This setup should be performed for each of the following templates: Homozygous normal ($\beta^{\mathrm{A}}/\beta^{\mathrm{A}}$) DNA, Heterozygous sickle cell trait ($\beta^{\mathrm{A}}/\beta^{\mathrm{S}}$) DNA, Homozygous sickle cell ($\beta^{\mathrm{S}}/\beta^{\mathrm{S}}$) DNA, $\beta$-thalassemia DNA ($\beta^{\mathrm{th}}/\beta^{\mathrm{th}}$), and a no-template Reagent Control.)

    Step 1.2: Assemble PCR reactions for Sickle Cell Allele ($\beta^{\mathrm{S}}$) detection.

        Option 1.2.1: Reaction Mix for Sickle Cell Allele-Specific Amplification.
            - Component A: KCl
                - Recipe: Final concentration of 50 mM.
            - Component B: Tris HCl
                - Recipe: Final concentration of 10 mM, pH 8.3.
            - Component C: MgCl₂
                - Recipe: Final concentration of 1.5 mM.
            - Component D: Gelatin
                - Recipe: Final concentration of 0.01% (wt/vol).
            - Component E: dNTPs (dATP, dCTP, dGTP, TTP)
                - Recipe: Final concentration of 0.1 mM of each nucleoside triphosphate.
            - Component F: HPβ14S
                - Recipe: Final concentration of 0.12 µM.
            - Component G: BGP2
                - Recipe: Final concentration of 0.12 µM.
            - Component H: GHPCR1
                - Recipe: Final concentration of 0.2 µM.
            - Component I: GHPCR2
                - Recipe: Final concentration of 0.2 µM.
            - Component J: *Taq* DNA polymerase
            - Component K: Template DNA / Control
                - Recipe: Added to a final concentration of 0.5 µg/ml for DNA samples. For the reagent control, water is added instead of DNA.
            (Operational details: Prepare a master mix containing components A-J and water, sufficient for the number of reactions. Aliquot the master mix into individual reaction tubes. Add the appropriate Template DNA or water (for reagent control) to each tube to bring the total volume to 50 µl. This setup should be performed for each of the following templates: Homozygous normal ($\beta^{\mathrm{A}}/\beta^{\mathrm{A}}$) DNA, Heterozygous sickle cell trait ($\beta^{\mathrm{A}}/\beta^{\mathrm{S}}$) DNA, Homozygous sickle cell ($\beta^{\mathrm{S}}/\beta^{\mathrm{S}}$) DNA, $\beta$-thalassemia DNA ($\beta^{\mathrm{th}}/\beta^{\mathrm{th}}$), and a no-template Reagent Control.)

Part 2: PCR Amplification

    Step 2.1: Perform thermal cycling.

        Option 2.1.1: Standard Amplification Protocol.
            - Component A: Assembled PCR Reactions from Part 1
            (Operational details: Place the reaction tubes in a thermal cycler and run the following program for 25 cycles:
            1. Heat-denaturation: 94°C for 1 min
            2. Annealing: 55°C for 2 min
            3. Polymerization: 72°C for 3 min
            After 25 cycles are complete, hold the samples at 4°C until ready for analysis.)

Part 3: Analysis of Amplification Products

    Step 3.1: Prepare PCR products for gel loading.

        Option 3.1.1: Mix PCR Product with Loading Buffer.
            - Component A: Amplified PCR products
            - Component B: 5x Ficoll loading buffer
            (Operational details: In a new tube or on a piece of parafilm, mix 15 µl of the amplified PCR product from each reaction with 5 µl of 5x Ficoll loading buffer. Mix gently by pipetting.)

    Step 3.2: Perform agarose gel electrophoresis.

        Option 3.2.1: Separation on a 1.5% Agarose Gel.
            - Component A: Prepared PCR samples for gel loading
            - Component B: 1.5% agarose gel
                - Recipe: Prepared using agarose powder in electrophoresis buffer.
            - Component C: Electrophoresis buffer
                - Recipe: 89 mM Tris-HCl, 89 mM borate, 2 mM EDTA.
            (Operational details: Submerge the 1.5% agarose gel in the electrophoresis buffer within a gel tank. Carefully load the entire volume of each prepared sample into separate wells of the gel. Run the electrophoresis for 2 hours at 120 V.)

    Step 3.3: Visualize DNA fragments.

        Option 3.3.1: Ethidium Bromide Staining and UV Trans-illumination.
            - Component A: Agarose gel post-electrophoresis
            - Component B: ethidium bromide staining solution
                - Recipe: 1.0 µg/ml ethidium bromide in water.
            - Component C: water
            (Operational details: After electrophoresis, carefully transfer the gel into the ethidium bromide staining solution and stain for 15 minutes. Subsequently, move the gel into a container with water and destain for 10 minutes. Place the destained gel on an ultraviolet trans-illuminator to visualize the DNA bands and photograph the results.)
